title: Tell me about a time you drove clarity on an ambiguous project
prompt: Tell me about a time the goal, responsibilities or information for a task were unclear. Explain how you made progress toward a shared understanding and what happened. The example can come from work, study or another responsibility.
blurb: Ambiguity (senior): did they impose structure on chaos and align others — or just wait for direction?

rubric.label: The ambiguity
rubric.description: Identifies what was unclear and why it affected a concrete task or decision.

rubric.label: Taking on the ambiguity
rubric.description: Explains their part in clarifying the problem, including seeking an appropriate owner or decision-maker rather than assuming authority.

rubric.label: Specific contribution and decisions
rubric.description: Describes specific questions, checks, decomposition or small experiments that reduced uncertainty and informed a next step.

rubric.label: Outcome and evidence
rubric.description: Describes a useful change in shared understanding, a decision, a handoff or an outcome; a document can be useful evidence when its purpose and use are explained.

rubric.label: Reflection & judgment
rubric.description: Explains remaining uncertainty, an assumption they revisited and when there was enough information to act or escalate.

rubric.label: Clear, relevant communication
rubric.description: Makes the relevant situation, reasoning and contribution understandable in any clear order. No required STAR structure, pronouns, performance of confidence or emotional tone.

reference.scenario: Explore an unclear brief, uncertain responsibility or conflicting information. A small handoff, assignment or service task can demonstrate the competency. Assess how uncertainty became an actionable understanding, not the size or prestige of the project.
model_points: Specifies the ambiguity rather than simply calling the task confusing.
Identifies what the candidate could clarify and who held the relevant decision authority.
Uses concrete questions, available evidence, a sketch or a small trial to narrow uncertainty.
Checks important assumptions with people affected and records an agreed next step where useful.
Describes what became clearer or what could proceed, accepting qualitative outcomes and useful intermediate work.
Acknowledges uncertainty that remained and describes a sensible review or escalation point.

probes.question: Which uncertainty most affected your next step?

probes.trigger: candidate describes a document but not its use
probes.question: How did someone use that document to make progress?
How did you check that others understood the plan?

red_flags: Presents an unresolved assumption as an agreed fact after being corrected.
Claims authority or agreement that their own account does not support.
Continues a potentially unsafe task despite recognizing that essential instructions are missing.
follow_ups: What information caused you to revise the plan?
Which uncertainty could safely remain open?
reference.exemplar_answer: Illustrative example only; it is not a required setting, answer order or achievement standard. Our class group was told to prepare a presentation but had different ideas about the audience. I listed the assumptions we disagreed on and asked the instructor which audience to use. We then agreed on three topics and recorded who would prepare each. A simple shared outline let us start work without duplicating it. I learned to resolve the uncertainty that changes the work before polishing a plan.
reference.assessment_contract: Assess the selected competency from concrete job-relevant evidence. Examples from paid work, study, volunteering, caregiving, informal work, military service and community activities are equally eligible when relevant. A modest example is sufficient if it shows the competency; employer prestige, formal title and financial scale are not criteria. Accept qualitative or quantitative outcomes supported by the account, including partial or unsuccessful outcomes. Do not require a numeric metric, STAR order, particular pronouns, composure, enthusiasm or a particular communication style. Identify personal contribution by meaning while preserving credit to others. Assess intelligibility and relevance, not accent, fluency, verbosity, visible emotion, disability or private circumstances. Mark genuinely missing evidence not assessed; do not infer poor competence or dishonesty from an absent example. A clearly labeled hypothetical may be discussed as situational practice but must not count as demonstrated past experience. Respect scope of practice, authorization, safety and ethical duties; pausing, declining, reporting or escalating can be sound judgment. Never require obedience, direct confrontation, unpaid overwork or successful persuasion regardless of the circumstances.
